name: build-and-deploy-memory-envelope
description: Compile, test, and run heavy parallel work inside the box's real memory envelope. Two silent host deaths during task-executor walks on a 7.6G machine (kernel/oomd kill, no panic logged) set this doctrine.
principles: Measure before parallelizing: MemAvailable (not free) is the launch signal; read /proc/meminfo at launch time.
One compile front at a time: release build, test suite, and per-pipeline fleets each own the machine serially; parallel fronts thrash CPU and blur the storage picture.
Disk floor 10G before ANY release link; prune build artifacts and regenerable caches only - never data islands (zsei_data, config, logs).
A silent death with no panic is memory until proven otherwise; dmesg/oomd first, code second.
heuristics: Before launching any walk fan-out: if MemAvailable < floor (default 1536MB), skip the tick loudly and retry next tick - refuse-to-launch beats silent death.
After any unexplained process death: check kernel/oomd logs, measure concurrent subprocess count at death time, and only then read the last code touched.
Parallel lanes scale with cores, launches scale with memory - gate each separately.

decision_rules.condition: launching a full orchestration walk or multi-process fan-out
decision_rules.action: Require MemAvailable >= floor; else skip loudly and retry next tick.

decision_rules.condition: disk free below 10G before a release link
decision_rules.action: Stop; prune build artifacts and regenerable caches; never data islands.
